source: I want to create an open world role playing experience for fans of Lord of The Rings. It will be a cozy game where players can tend to their gardens, trade vegetables, and explore the idyllic nature around with their friends. I want the game to be set up in the Shire. For my first map, I want to create Hobbiton, where players will have their own hobbit burrows. Can you create a realistic replica of Hobbiton?

image_prompt.text: Hobbit burrows dug into the grassy mounds with round doors and windows, each one enterable and claimable by a player as their own home
The village centre of Hobbiton - an oversized green with market stalls where players gather to trade vegetables and produce
Winding dirt lanes linking the green to the burrows and garden plots, sized for foot traffic rather than vehicles
The idyllic countryside around the village - rolling green hills, hedgerows and open meadow to wander through with friends

layout_placement.text: Planting plots beside each burrow where players tend and harvest their vegetable gardens
The vegetables themselves as gatherable crops the trading loop runs on

notes: Claimable rather than buildable housing: the prompt says players have their own hobbit burrows, which are pre-built and dug into the hills, not lots they construct on. Enterable burrows make this P3.
Gardening and crop trading are Simulation's task-station and extractable-resource options brought in as a secondary genre; Roleplay has no way to express a garden you tend.
The user calls this the first map of a larger open world, so the boundary of Hobbiton should read as a valley that continues rather than a hard edge.

open_questions.ask: How many burrows should Hobbiton hold? That sets whether this is a 500-stud village or a 2000-stud valley.
Do players claim an existing burrow, or dig and customise their own?

theme: High Fantasy (cozy pastoral - green hills, round doors, no heroic or grim register)

coverage_missing.ask: How many player burrows should the village support?
Are burrows claimed as-is, or customisable inside?
Is there progression behind the gardening - seasons, seed unlocks, coin - or is it purely social?

answers.ask: How many burrows should Hobbiton hold? That sets whether this is a 500-stud village or a 2000-stud valley.
answers.answer: Build a compact 500-stud Hobbiton village with around 12 player burrows; keep it cozy and easy to explore with friends.

answers.ask: Do players claim an existing burrow, or dig and customise their own?
answers.answer: Players should claim one of the existing hobbit burrows, with simple customization of their garden and interior rather than digging new burrows.
